I will keep my land mostly in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is what I know best, it matches my well irrigation, and on 5 mu I need a steady grain harvest with work I can still manage at 71. I will put 4 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 4 mu, and I will keep 1 mu for cotton because I have long experience with it and it spreads my risk a little. I will not chase very high input use. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it gives me more stable emergence and yield, but I will keep fertilizer and spraying at a level I can afford and manage by hand. For wheat I will aim for a solid stand, enough nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, and three irrigations because I have a well. After wheat harvest, I will quickly seed maize on the same land, use hybrid seed, give it the heaviest nitrogen among my crops, and irrigate mainly at the key growth stages. For cotton, I will keep one mu only, use improved seed, fertilize more evenly with some extra potassium, irrigate a few times, and spray more than for grain because insects and disease are usually a bigger problem there. I will mostly use rotary tillage because the area is small and it saves me labor while still giving me a workable seedbed.
